title: Composure at the Hungaroring
excerpt: A composed drive through a difficult weekend secured another podium — and kept AMER at the top of the championship.
heroAlt: AMER in the garage before the race
body:
The Hungaroring never gives anyone a comfortable Sunday. Track temperatures sat above 48°C, the field was separated by less than eight tenths in qualifying, and AMER started sixth on a grid where position is everything.

The plan was simple and brutal: survive lap one, keep the tyres alive through the opening stint, and attack in the final ten laps when everyone else's rears gave up. It worked. A clean pit window on lap 22 jumped two cars in the pitlane, and a composed final stint on hard compounds brought the BMW home third.

"This is a podium that feels like a win," AMER said parc fermé. "We lost pace on Saturday and recovered everything on Sunday. The team was flawless."

The result keeps AMER at the top of the championship with 201 points and an 11-point lead heading into the next round — a circuit where the F10's low-drag setup should come alive.

title: Silverstone in the wet: from P8 to P4
excerpt: A lap-one puncture turned the British round into a recovery drive — and proved the privateer's racecraft is already elite.
heroAlt: AMER walking the pit lane in team kit
body:
Contact at Copse on lap one left AMER with a right-rear puncture and the entire field streaming past. By the time the car limped back to the pits, P8 had become P19.

What followed was the drive of the weekend: twelve positions recovered in mixed conditions, including a double overtake around the outside of Stowe that the crowd rewarded with a roar loud enough to cut through the onboard audio.

Twelve points for P4, and a clear message: nothing is lost until the chequered flag.

title: Suzuka: the first victory
excerpt: Pole position, a lights-to-flag win, and the fastest lap — AMER's first victory came exactly the way he dreamed it would.
heroAlt: The BMW F10 535i on track at Suzuka
body:
Everything happened on Saturday. A lap through 130R at the limit put the F10 on pole by eleven thousandths, and the nerves that followed all night were the good kind.

Sunday was a masterclass in controlled aggression. AMER led every one of the 53 laps, managed a mid-race safety car without losing the lead, and sealed the victory with the fastest lap two laps from the end.

The first victory interview is always a blur. "I don't remember what I said," AMER admitted afterwards. "I just remember my family crying."

The paddock woke up to its first winner of the season.

title: Building a season that lasts
excerpt: Why the 2026 campaign is being built around consistency, not highlights — and why that starts with the people around the car.
heroAlt: AMER beside the BMW F10 in the garage
body:
Seasons are lost in two ways: by crashing, or by trying not to. The 2026 programme is built to avoid both.

The winter focused on physical conditioning and on race-start simulations, where clean clutch engagement matters more than raw reaction time. Around the car, the crew has been deliberately kept stable. Same engineers, same mechanics, same briefing rhythm.

"Consistency in the garage creates consistency on track," says AMER. "We don't need new ideas on a Sunday. We need the right ones, every time."

Twelve rounds in, the points say the plan is working.
